data.body_html:
If you’re looking for the best snorkeling spots near Marbella by boat, two names come up again and again: Cabopino and Estepona. Both offer clear Mediterranean water, marine life, and easy anchorage—but they suit different preferences. This guide compares the two, so you can choose the right spot for your 2041 charter from [Puerto Banús](/).

Cabopino: Sandy Coves for Beginners

Cabopino lies 15 nautical miles west of Puerto Banús, about a 30-40 minute cruise on most powerboats. The seabed here is mostly sand with patches of Posidonia seagrass, keeping water visibility at 10-15m in summer. Depths range from 2-5m, making it safe for children and less confident swimmers.

The main snorkeling area is the cove just east of the Cabopino marina breakwater. You’ll find seabream, damselfish, and the occasional octopus hiding under rocks. There are no currents to speak of, and the shoreline is backed by dunes and pine trees—a relaxed vibe.

Estepona: Rocky Reefs for Experienced Snorkelers

Estepona is 20 NM from Puerto Banús, adding 15-20 minutes each way. The snorkeling here is more dramatic: rocky outcrops, artificial reef structures, and deeper water (5-12m). Visibility often reaches 15-20m, and the marine life is richer—groupers, moray eels, and sometimes rays.

The best spot is the Punta Doncella reef, just west of Estepona’s port. You’ll need to be a confident swimmer; there’s no beach exit, so you’ll enter and exit from the boat. We provide buoyancy aids and fins, but it’s not ideal for young children.

Boat Options for Your Snorkeling Trip

Both destinations are easily reachable from Puerto Banús. For speed, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) hits 30+ knots and includes a free jet ski—great for exploring coves between dives. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers plenty of deck space for sunbathing and a shaded flybridge.

What’s Included in Your Charter

Every snorkeling charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and all safety equipment. We also provide snorkel masks, fins, and buoyancy aids. Onboard you’ll find water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks—all included in the price. Spanish IVA (21%) is included too.

For the Mangusta 80 (Tier B, from €4,719 for 4 hours), a jet ski is included free. For other boats, pricing is available on request via WhatsApp.

Best Time for Snorkeling in Marbella

The snorkeling season runs June to September, when water temperatures hit 22-26°C and the sea is calmest. May and October are also good but cooler (18-21°C). Avoid November to March—water drops to 14-16°C, and winds can make the sea choppy.

Visibility is best in July and August, often exceeding 15m at both spots. Early morning (9-11am) is ideal: the water is clearest, and there are fewer boats.

Which Spot Should You Choose?

Pick Cabopino if you’re bringing children, want a relaxed beach-style snorkel, or prefer shallow sandy bottoms. Pick Estepona if you’re an experienced snorkeler, want to see bigger marine life, and don’t mind a longer boat ride.

If you have time, do both on a day charter: start at Cabopino, then head west to Estepona for lunch and a second dive. The total round trip from Puerto Banús is about 45 NM—easily doable in 6-8 hours.
